resources.string: LTE Mapper needs your location to tag every signal measurement with GPS coordinates so it can draw the coverage map. Location is never uploaded anywhere.
LTE Mapper needs phone-state access to read cell signal information (RSRP, RSRQ, cell ID, operator) from the modem. No calls, contacts, or personal data are ever read.
Allow \"all the time\" location access if you want mapping to continue while the screen is off or the app is in the background.
Android requires a visible notification while LTE Mapper collects measurements in the background, so you always know mapping is active.
Permission denied. You can grant it later from system Settings.

LTE Mapper only stores data locally on this device.

 What is collected: GPS coordinates, GPS accuracy, and cellular signal parameters (RSRP, RSRQ, SNR, cell ID, PCI, EARFCN, operator, network type) while a mapping session is running.

 Why it is collected: to build a signal-strength map of the areas you visit and let you review coverage history and statistics.

 Where it is stored: in a local Room/SQLite database inside this app's private storage. Nothing is uploaded to any server, and there is no analytics or tracking of any kind.

 How to export it: use Settings → Export to save your measurements as CSV, GeoJSON, or KML files you control.

 How to delete it: use the button below to permanently erase all recorded sessions and measurements from this device.
This permanently deletes every mapping session and measurement stored on this device. This cannot be undone.
Android can pause location and background mapping to save battery. Exempting LTE Mapper keeps long or screen-off sessions running reliably.
